companyIntro.name: Northwind Commercial
companyIntro.mission: Grow B2B revenue through honest selling and disciplined pipeline management.
companyIntro.culture: Customers first, forecasts honest. A deal is only real when the buyer has a reason and a date.

projectBackground.name: Enterprise Pipeline Rebuild
projectBackground.context: The pipeline looks large but the forecast has missed twice. The sales director wants a realistic number.

manager.name: Elin Berg
manager.note: A big pipeline isn't a forecast. Give me the weighted number and the one deal you're most worried about.

assignment.title: Build an honest forecast
assignment.brief: Calculate funnel wins and deals needed, weight the pipeline in Excel, qualify opportunities and write a follow-up email.

documents.name: Open Deals
documents.note: Three open deals with values and probabilities.

tasks.title: Funnel Wins
tasks.prompt: 1,000 leads, 20% qualified, 25% of those receive a proposal, 40% of proposals win. How many deals are won?
tasks.mistake: Using the first rate only overstates wins.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Deals Needed
tasks.prompt: The target is €600,000 and the average deal is €15,000. How many deals are needed?
tasks.mistake: Ignoring the gap (20 vs 40) makes the forecast fantasy.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Discovery
tasks.prompt: What is the best opening in a discovery call?
options: Ask open questions about the buyer's problem and impact
tasks.mistake: Pitching first misses the real need.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Discount Request
tasks.prompt: The buyer asks for 20% off immediately. What is a good response?
options: Ask what they need and trade discount for value such as volume or term
tasks.reasoning: Concessions should be traded, not given.
tasks.mistake: Free concessions erode margin and credibility.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Weighted Pipeline (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Weighted value in column D = B x C. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: Weighted pipeline is an honest forecast.
tasks.mistake: Summing raw values inflates the forecast.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Follow-up Email
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence follow-up email after a discovery call.
tasks.modelAnswer: Hi Anna, thank you for the time today. You mentioned that manual order entry costs your team about ten hours a week and delays shipments. I will send a short proposal by Friday showing how we can cut that, with a two-week pilot. Would Thursday at 10:00 work for a 20-minute review? If anything changes before then, let me know.
tasks.reasoning: A good follow-up recalls the buyer's problem, states next steps and proposes a date.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Pipeline That Was Always Full
caseStudy.background: A team reported a €3M pipeline each quarter but closed only €400,000. Most deals had no next step or decision date.
caseStudy.challenges: Deals stayed in pipeline without qualification.
questions: How do you keep the forecast honest?
caseStudy.solution: Northwind required a next step and decision date for every deal and weekly pipeline reviews.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Qualify hard; a deal needs a reason and a date.

options: A next step and decision date

prompts: Which deal would you worry about first?
